## Why one listing at a time is best now

Because each Google Groups/Gmail listing may have different problems:

```text
old price
updated reply
missing land size
different image format
duplicate listing
agent phone in weird format
inline images instead of attachments
multiple replies in one conversation
```

The current project notes also say Google Groups posts may contain repeated replies/updates, so the parser should not blindly use the first or latest message. It should use the message with full specs, price, description, and images.

```text
3. Create draft-listing.json

6. Put optimized images in optimized/
7. Create/update notes.md
```

That removes most of the tedious work while keeping control.

```text
auto-approve AI result
```

Because Phase 1 and Phase 2 are not separate businesses. They are two parts of one automation pipeline.

Your own data-extractor plan already shows the later flow: draft listing generation, Google Sheets approval, then future publishing automation only after the approval phase is stable. 

The agent map also shows the same logic: email fetcher → parser → image organizer → draft generator → Google Sheets draft → human review → future publisher → live website.

## But each phase should still have its own folder

This handles:

```text

source.txt
raw email JSON
AI parsing
draft-listing.json
image rename
image optimization
Google Sheets draft
human review
```

This phase touches sensitive raw data, emails, attachments, logs, and unapproved listing information.

### Phase 2 — Website Uploader

This handles:

```text
approved draft JSON
approved optimized images
website data/listings.json
image paths
sitemap update
listing page update
deployment later
```

This phase should only touch **approved data**, not raw emails.

That separation is important for privacy and safety. The auto-upload policy already says AI outputs must be treated as drafts and that no listing should be published without explicit human approval.

Put the main legal and safety documents at the **root parent folder**, because they apply to the whole automation project.

```text
├── EMAIL-EXTRACTION-POLICY.md
├── AUTOMATION-SAFETY-POLICY.md
```

Then inside each phase folder, the `README.md` can say:

```text
This module follows the root project privacy, data handling, and automation safety policies.
```

This avoids duplicating legal files in both phase folders.

## My recommended decision

Use this:

```text
One parent repository:
jkpro-property-automation

With two phase folders:
phase-1-data-extractor
phase-2-website-uploader
```

Keep the actual website project separate for now:

```text
PROPERTI_WEBSITE/
jkpro-property-automation/
```

Why? Because your current website is already its own static catalog project. The automation project should generate approved output that can later be copied or pushed into the website project.

Later, when the automation is stable, you can connect them more tightly.

## The safest current architecture

```text
PROPERTI_WEBSITE/
  data/listings.json
  images/
  index.html
  listings.html
  property.html

jkpro-property-automation/
  phase-1-data-extractor/
    creates draft-listing.json
    creates optimized images

  phase-2-website-uploader/
    takes approved draft-listing.json
    copies into PROPERTI_WEBSITE/data/listings.json
    copies images into PROPERTI_WEBSITE/images/
```

This is clean, safe, and realistic.

So yes: **Phase 1 and Phase 2 should be in one automation project folder**, but the **website itself can remain a separate project folder** for now.

Phases stay isolated — Phase 1 and Phase 2 each own their scripts and output, so a bug or broken script in one phase cannot accidentally touch the other phase's files.

### 2. `transaction_type` is null, but the listing should probably be `dijual`

and add:

The extractor should **not automatically assume filename mismatch means wrong images**.

## About the Git tag

This command:

```powershell
git tag -a v0.3.0 -m "Local draft extractor baseline"
```

creates a named checkpoint called `v0.3.0`.

It does **not** upload anything. It does **not** change files. It just marks the current commit as an important milestone.

I recommend doing the tag **after** committing the regression tests, because the tests are important protection for the v0.3.0 baseline.

## Very important note about Google Groups

Google Groups pages may require your browser login. A normal Python `requests` script may fail because it cannot access your logged-in Google session.

So there are two possible methods:

### Method 1 — Browser-assisted manual export, easiest and safest

You open the Google Groups listing page yourself, then use a helper script/bookmarklet/browser-save method to collect text/images from the visible page.

This avoids Gmail API and avoids bulk scraping.

### Method 2 — Playwright browser automation

A script opens a real browser window, you log in manually if needed, then it extracts the visible listing page.

This is more automatic but more complex.

For your current level, I recommend **Method 1 first**, then Playwright later.

## Best current workflow

For now, the best practical workflow is:

```text

2. Save/copy the visible listing text into source.txt

4. Run process_listing.py
5. Review notes.md
```

```text
3. It creates source.txt and downloads images
4. Then process_listing.py continues
```

```text
4. Script extracts text + local images from that saved page.
5. Script creates draft-imports/listing-code/source.txt and original/.
```

This is safer than trying to log into Google automatically.

So, to answer your question clearly:

The method before was:

```text
Manual/semi-automatic one-listing folder preparation
```

```text
One Google Groups listing page importer
```


is probably not fully public. Your browser can see it because you are logged in, but a Python script using `requests` usually cannot.

So the realistic options are:

## Option 1 — Best simple method: browser-assisted extractor

This means:

```text
You open the Google Groups listing in Chrome
↓
You click a local bookmarklet / browser helper

↓
```

```text
↓
Click a local Chrome extension button: “Extract JKPRO Listing”
↓
Extension extracts visible listing text
↓
Extension finds visible attachment/image links
↓
Extension downloads images using your logged-in browser session
↓
Extension saves/copies source text
↓
Local tool processes the folder
```

This is better than Python `requests`, because Google Groups requires your logged-in browser session.

## Why a Chrome extension is likely the best path

A Chrome extension can work inside the Google Groups page that you already opened. It can use your logged-in browser state without asking for Gmail API or Google Groups API.

It also avoids:

```text
❌ bulk scraping 700 listings
❌ login automation
❌ Gmail API setup
❌ Google Groups API setup
❌ typing long terminal commands
❌ clicking 50 download buttons manually
```

It keeps the safe constraint:

```text
✅ one opened listing page at a time
✅ user is already logged in
✅ user chooses what listing to process
✅ no auto-publish
✅ human review still required
```

## Important limitation

A Chrome extension may not be able to save directly into:

```text
phase1_properti_auto_data_extractor/draft-imports/listing-code/
```

without extra permission or a native helper.

So the first version should download into your browser Downloads folder, for example:

```text
Downloads/JKPRO-Extracts/tanah-bekasi-003/
├── source.txt
└── original/
    ├── tanah-bekasi-003-001.jpg
    ├── tanah-bekasi-003-002.jpg
    └── ...
```

Then the local import assistant can import that folder into the project.

Later, if needed, we can make a native desktop/local app that saves directly to the project folder.

Build a **Chrome extension MVP**:

```text
@phase1_properti_auto_data_extractor/browser-tools/chrome-extension/
```

```text
3. Extract visible message text
4. Extract image/attachment URLs
5. Download source.txt
6. Download images into a named folder

```

# chatgpt response

We **can** go straight toward software. The reason I suggested Chrome extension first is because the hardest part is not the software UI — it is **getting Google Groups images automatically while you are logged in**.

A normal desktop software cannot easily access the images from Google Groups because Google Groups depends on your Chrome login/session. A local Python app outside the browser usually cannot see those private attachment links unless we add complicated login/cookie handling, which is risky and fragile.

So the best “straight to software” design is actually:

```text
Chrome extension = extraction button inside logged-in Google Groups
Local software = receives/imports extracted source.txt + images, processes them, and prepares website-ready output
```

## Why not only local desktop software?

A local desktop app can easily do:

```text
create listing folder
run process_listing.py
optimize images
show draft JSON
show notes
later export to website
```

But it cannot easily do this:

```text
open private Google Groups attachment image
download 50 images using your logged-in Google account
```

unless we use one of these risky/complex methods:

```text
1. Ask for Google login/cookies
2. Use browser automation with your logged-in profile
3. Use Gmail/Google API
4. Use a Chrome extension
```

The safest and simplest of those is the **Chrome extension**, because it runs inside the browser page you already opened and logged into.

## Best direct-to-software plan

Instead of thinking “extension vs software,” think of it as one local tool system:

```text
JKPRO Property Automation Tool
├── Browser extraction part
│   └── Chrome extension button on Google Groups
│
└── Local desktop/helper part
    ├── imports extracted files
    ├── runs parser
    ├── optimizes images
    ├── shows notes
    └── later exports to website
```

So yes, you can build “software,” but the Google Groups extraction part should still be browser-based.

## Recommended staged software path

### Stage 1 — Chrome extension MVP

Goal:

```text
Open one Google Groups listing
Click “Extract”
Download:
- source.txt
- original images
```

This solves your biggest pain: downloading many images one by one.

### Stage 2 — Local software/assistant MVP

Goal:

```text
Open local app
Choose downloaded listing folder
Click “Process”
It creates:
- draft-listing.json
- optimized images
- notes.md
```

This removes terminal commands.

### Stage 3 — Full local desktop workflow

Goal:

```text
Open app
See imported listings
Review extracted data
Approve
Export to website project
Preview website
```

At this stage you mostly do not need VS Code for daily use.

### Stage 4 — Phase 2 website uploader

Goal:

```text
Approved draft
↓
copy optimized images into website
↓
update data/listings.json
↓
validate JSON
↓
preview locally
↓
manual deploy / later semi-auto deploy
```

## The practical answer

Yes, go toward software — but do **not** skip the browser extraction layer.

The best first “software” should be:

```text
Chrome extension + local processing script
```

not a standalone desktop app only.

## What I recommend building next

Build the Chrome extension first, because it handles the part that desktop software cannot easily handle: **using your logged-in Google Groups page to extract images**.

Then immediately after that, build a local UI/wizard so you do not need terminal commands.

So the next order should be:

```text
1. Chrome extension: one-click extract text + images from current Google Groups listing
2. Local assistant/software: process extracted folder
3. Phase 2 uploader: export approved listing to website
```

## If you want to go “more software-like” immediately

We can ask Codex to create a simple local app folder now, but still include the Chrome extension as the extraction module.

Project structure could become:

```text
phase1_properti_auto_data_extractor/
├── browser-tools/
│   └── chrome-extension/
│
├── local-app/
│   ├── app.py
│   ├── README.md
│   └── templates/
│
├── scripts/
│   ├── process_listing.py
│   ├── import_assistant.py
│   └── import_saved_google_groups_page.py
```

The local app can be a simple local web app at first:

```text
python local-app/app.py
```

Then open:

```text
http://localhost:5000
```

Buttons:

```text
Import Extracted Folder
Run Processor
Open Notes
Open Draft JSON
```

But for image extraction from Google Groups, the extension still does the first part.

## My recommendation

Do this next:

```text
Build Chrome extension MVP first.
Then build local app MVP second.
```

Because without automatic image extraction, the local software will still depend on manually downloading 20–50 images, which is the tedious part you most want to solve.

# chatgpt response

Yes — the Python processing can be automated **after the Edge/Chrome extension extracts the listing**.

Right now the workflow is:

```text
1. Open Google Groups listing
2. Click extension
3. Extension downloads:
   Downloads/JKPRO-Extracts/[listing-code]/source.txt
   Downloads/JKPRO-Extracts/[listing-code]/original/images
4. Manually copy folder into draft-imports/
5. Manually run process_listing.py
```

The next improvement should make steps 4 and 5 automatic.

## Best next workflow

After the extension downloads the folder, you run one simple command:

```powershell
python scripts\process_extension_export.py tanah-bekasi-005
```

Then it automatically:

```text
1. Finds Downloads/JKPRO-Extracts/tanah-bekasi-005
2. Copies it into draft-imports/tanah-bekasi-005
3. Runs process_listing.py
4. Creates draft-listing.json
5. Creates notes.md
6. Creates optimized WebP images
7. Prints summary
```

Later, this can become even easier:

```powershell
python scripts\process_extension_export.py --latest
```

or eventually a local app button:

```text
Process Latest Extension Export
```

## Important: fix parser issues too

Your `pondok-melati-001` result is mostly okay, but `pondok-gede-001` shows parser problems:

```text
property_type = tanah
```

But the title says:

```text
RUMAH SECOND MURAH TANAH LUAS SIAP HUNI...
```

That should be `rumah`, not `tanah`. The parser saw “TANAH LUAS” and over-classified it as land, even though the listing is a house.

Also wrong:

```text
agent_name = IMAGE URLS
agent_phone = 6220250713
```

So before making the workflow fully automatic, we should fix these parser mistakes. Otherwise the automation will be fast, but sometimes wrong.

## Recommended order

Do this next:

```text
1. Fix parser bugs from pondok-gede-001
2. Add process_extension_export.py to automate copy + processing
3. Later create a local app button for the same process
```

# chatgpt response

Yes, let’s clarify.

## Does the extension auto-run the Python script?

**No, not yet.**

Right now the workflow is:

```text
1. Edge extension extracts listing
2. Edge extension downloads source.txt + images
3. You run Python script manually:
   python scripts\process_extension_export.py [listing-code]
```

The extension **cannot directly run Python automatically** because browser extensions are sandboxed. Edge/Chrome does not allow an extension to freely run local `.py` files for security reasons.

To make it fully automatic later, we need one of these:

```text
Option A: Local app/server running in background
Extension sends the listing code to local app
Local app runs Python

Option B: Native messaging host
More advanced Chrome/Edge extension integration

Option C: Keep one-command processing
Extension downloads → you run one short command
```

For now, we are at **Option C**.

The error says:

```text

C:\Users\HP\Downloads\JKPRO-Extracts
```

That means `process_extension_export.py` is looking here:

```text
C:\Users\HP\Downloads\JKPRO-Extracts
```

But your Edge extension probably downloaded the files somewhere else.


or another custom Edge download location.

The website listing schema is clear now:

```text
id
```

## Important mapping for Phase 2

The exporter should map Phase 1 → website like this:

```text
property_type rumah → type house
property_type ruko → type commercial
property_type apartemen → type apartment
property_type tanah → type land

price_number → price
price_text → priceLabel
building_area_m2 → area
land_area_m2 → landSize
certificate_type → certificate
water_source → waterSource
agent_name / agent_phone → agent
optimized/*.webp → images/properties/[slug]/optimized/[slug]-001.webp
```

For `status`, the website uses:

```text
for-sale
```

So Phase 2 should use:

```text
transaction_type dijual → status for-sale
transaction_type disewa/sewa → status for-rent
```

For now, if uncertain, default to `for-sale` only after human review.

## Do we still need the tree?

Yes, but only a focused tree. Please run this next:

```powershell
tree properti_website\images\properties /F
```

and:

```powershell
tree properti_automation-v0.3.0\phase2_properti_auto_upload /F
```

This will tell us:
1. how image folders are currently named, and
2. what Phase 2 already contains.

After that, I will give you the final precise Codex prompt for Phase 2 MVP.

```text
- Keep this one approved listing at a time.
- Human review is required before export.

Current folder context:
Parent workspace:
@properti-projects

@properti_automation-v0.3.0

@properti_automation-v0.3.0/phase2_properti_auto_upload
It currently has scripts/.gitkeep and existing planning/data model docs.

Goal:
Create a safe script that exports one approved Phase 1 draft listing into the existing static property website format.

Create:
@properti_automation-v0.3.0/phase2_properti_auto_upload/scripts/export_to_website.py

Update:
@properti_automation-v0.3.0/phase2_properti_auto_upload/README.md

Create tests:
@properti_automation-v0.3.0/phase2_properti_auto_upload/tests/test_export_to_website.py

Command examples:

Dry-run:
python scripts/export_to_website.py --draft ../phase1_properti_auto_data_extractor/draft-imports/rumah-jaksel-001 --website "../../../properti_website"

Apply:
python scripts/export_to_website.py --draft ../phase1_properti_auto_data_extractor/draft-imports/rumah-jaksel-001 --website "../../../properti_website" --apply

Required behavior:

1. Default behavior must be dry-run:
   - Show what would be added/copied.
   - Do not modify website files.
   - Do not copy images.
   - Do not edit listings.json.

2. Apply behavior:
   - Only modify website when --apply is provided.
   - Before modifying data/listings.json, create timestamped backup:
     @properti_website/data/listings.backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.json
   - Append one listing object to data/listings.json.
   - Copy optimized WebP images from draft optimized/ into:
     @properti_website/images/properties/[slug]/optimized/
   - Do not copy original images yet in MVP unless you choose to add --copy-originals. The live website uses optimized WebP paths.

3. Validate draft folder:
   Refuse export if:
   - draft-listing.json is missing
   - notes.md is missing
   - optimized/ folder is missing
   - optimized/ has no .webp images
   - needs_review is not empty, unless --allow-review is provided

4. Read website listings:
   - Load @properti_website/data/listings.json
   - Validate it is a list
   - Determine new id as max existing numeric id + 1

5. Determine slug:
   - Use draft listing_code as slug by default.
   - If draft has a slug field, use it only if safe.
   - Slug must contain lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.
   - Refuse duplicate slug unless --force is provided.
   - Refuse if destination image folder already exists unless --force is provided.

6. Map Phase 1 draft fields to website schema.

Existing website schema fields include:
- id
- slug
- title
- status
- featured
- price
- priceLabel
- priceNote
- location
- locationArea
- locationCity
- province
- mapUrl
- type
- listingCategory
- area
- areaUnit
- landSize
- bedrooms
- bathrooms
- floors
- carport
- garage
- electricity
- waterSource
- certificate
- orientation
- accessRoad
- description
- promo
- features
- nearbyFacilities
- availableUnits
- images
- youtubeUrl
- virtualTourUrl
- agent
- seoTitle
- seoDescription
- keywords

Mapping rules:
- draft listing_code -> slug if no explicit slug
- draft title -> title
- draft price_number -> price
- draft price_text -> priceLabel
- priceNote -> "Harga buka" if price_text includes "HARGA BUKA", otherwise ""
- transaction_type "dijual" -> status "for-sale"
- transaction_type "disewa" or "sewa" -> status "for-rent"
- default status: "for-sale" only if transaction_type is dijual or if --allow-review is provided
- featured -> false
- property_type "rumah" -> type "house"
- property_type "ruko" -> type "commercial"
- property_type "apartemen" -> type "apartment"
- property_type "tanah" -> type "land"
- listingCategory -> "second" by default for extracted Google Groups listings
- building_area_m2 -> area
- areaUnit -> "m²"
- land_area_m2 -> landSize
- bedrooms -> bedrooms
- bathrooms -> bathrooms
- floors -> floors
- carport -> carport
- garage -> garage
- electricity should be numeric if possible:
  "1300 Watt" -> 1300
  null stays null
- water_source -> waterSource
- certificate_type -> certificate
- location_raw -> location
- Try to infer locationCity from location_raw using known Indonesian area names if easy:
  if contains "JAKARTA SELATAN" -> "Jakarta Selatan"
  if contains "BEKASI" -> "Bekasi"
  if contains "DEPOK" -> "Depok"
  otherwise ""
- locationArea may be location_raw title-cased or ""
- province:
  if location city contains Jakarta -> "DKI Jakarta"
  if Bekasi/Depok -> "Jawa Barat"
  otherwise ""
- mapUrl -> ""
- orientation -> ""
- accessRoad -> ""
- description -> generate a conservative description from extracted fields:
  Include title, land/building size, bedrooms/bathrooms, floors, certificate, water, electricity, and price. Do not invent facts.
- promo -> ""
- features -> [] for MVP unless safe features are parsed from draft/source
- nearbyFacilities -> [] for MVP unless safe nearby facilities are parsed from draft/source
- availableUnits -> null
- images -> list using:
  images/properties/[slug]/optimized/[slug]-001.webp
  images/properties/[slug]/optimized/[slug]-002.webp
  etc.
- youtubeUrl -> ""
- virtualTourUrl -> ""
- agent:
  name -> draft agent_name or ""
  phone -> draft agent_phone or ""
  role -> "Marketing"
- seoTitle -> conservative title + price label if available
- seoDescription -> short conservative summary from fields
- keywords -> conservative generated keywords from type, city/location, and title words

7. Image copy rules:
   - Source: draft optimized/*.webp
   - Destination: website/images/properties/[slug]/optimized/
   - Destination file names should be normalized:
     [slug]-001.webp
     [slug]-002.webp
   - In dry-run, only print what would be copied.
   - In apply mode, copy images.
   - Never delete existing website images.
   - Never overwrite existing image folder unless --force is provided.

8. Safety:
   - never deploy
   - never touch Cloudflare
   - never touch deploy/
   - never delete files
   - never modify website unless --apply
   - never export if needs_review exists unless --allow-review
   - create backup before modifying listings.json
   - validate JSON after writing
   - one listing only

9. Print summary:
   - mode: dry-run/apply
   - draft folder
   - website folder
   - new id
   - slug
   - website type
   - status
   - priceLabel
   - image count
   - destination image folder
   - whether listings.json would be changed / was changed
   - whether backup would be created / was created
   - warnings or refusal reason

10. Tests:
   Add tests for:
   - dry-run does not modify website files
   - apply appends one listing
   - duplicate slug is refused
   - non-empty needs_review is refused unless --allow-review
   - optimized images are copied on apply
   - listings.json backup is created on apply
   - property type mapping works for rumah/ruko/apartemen/tanah
   - electricity string "1300 Watt" becomes 1300
   - website listing JSON remains valid after apply

11. Run tests:
python -m unittest discover -s phase2_properti_auto_upload/tests -v

After creating:
```

```text
should become something like:
"Tanah Luas Dijual Murah Cocok untuk Investasi Lokasi Strategis di Ciketing Mustika Jaya Kota Bekasi"

Rules:
- Convert all-caps source text into readable Indonesian title case.
- Keep common small words lowercase when not first word:
  di, ke, dari, untuk, dan, yang, dengan, dekat, dalam
- Preserve known acronyms/terms:
  SHM, IMB, SHGB, HGB, AJB, PPJB, KPR, PLN, PAM, PDAM, LT, LB, KT, KM, SPBU, ATM
- Preserve units:
  m², M²

locationArea: "Ciketing Mustika Jaya"
locationCity: "Bekasi"
province: "Jawa Barat"

Rules:
- Remove marketing prefixes when present:
  "STRATEGIS DI "
  "LOKASI STRATEGIS DI "
  "ASRI DAN NYAMAN DI "
  "LOKASI "
- If contains "KOTA BEKASI" or "BEKASI", infer city "Bekasi".
- If contains "JAKARTA SELATAN", infer city "Jakarta Selatan".
- If contains "DEPOK", infer city "Depok".
- If city is known, remove city words from locationArea where practical.
- Convert locationArea to readable title case.
- Compose location as "[locationArea], [locationCity]" if both exist.
- If uncertain, keep existing safe fallback.

- Do not invent features or nearby facilities.

- Use readable title, not ALL CAPS.
- Keep it reasonably short if possible.
- Include priceLabel if available.
- Example:

Rules:
- Use readable casing.
- Include type, location, LT/LB if available, and price.
- Keep conservative and not too long.
- Do not invent facts.
```

# chatgpt response

Yes, you are thinking in the right direction. The terminal commands are okay for MVP/testing, but they are becoming tedious. The next priority should slowly move from “many manual commands” into “guided command menu / button UI,” while still keeping the system safe.

## Priority order from now

### Priority 1 — Keep exporting listings one by one using the proven flow

This stays highest priority because the main goal is still getting real listings into the website safely.

Current safe flow:

```text
1. Pick new Google Groups listing.
2. Use Edge extension.
3. Verify exact export folder name.
4. Process exact folder name, not --latest.
5. Inspect draft.
6. Manually fix needs_review.
7. Phase 2 dry-run.
8. Apply only if dry-run is clean.
9. Preview website.
10. Commit and tag.
```

For now, this is still the “main production flow.”

### Priority 2 — Add a small command-menu helper

Before making a full UI, I recommend a **terminal menu script** first.

Something like:

```text
JKPRO Automation Helper

1. List newest Edge export folders
2. Process selected export folder
3. Inspect draft summary
4. Run Phase 2 dry-run
5. Apply Phase 2 export
6. Validate website listing images
7. Show git status for both repos
8. Print next safe checklist
```

This is easier and safer than building a full app UI immediately. It reduces memorizing commands, but still keeps you aware of what is happening.

Best next development task:

```text
Create scripts/jkpro_helper.py
```

or maybe:

```text
tools/jkpro_menu.py
```

It should **not automatically apply/export without confirmation**. For dangerous steps like `--apply`, it should ask:

```text
Are you sure? Type APPLY to continue:
```

### Priority 3 — Add preflight validation before apply

Before every `--apply`, the helper should check:

```text
- website git status is clean
- draft exists
- needs_review is empty
- image count > 0
- slug does not already exist
- destination image folder does not already exist
- agent phone is safe
- locationCity/province are not blank
```

This prevents mistakes before they happen.

### Priority 4 — Add update-existing-listing mode

Right now Phase 2 is mostly append-focused. Later, you will need:

```text
update existing listing by slug
```

Example use cases:

```text
- fix title
- fix floor count
- fix phone number
- update price
- add more images
- fix location text
```

This should come after the helper menu, because update mode can be risky if not controlled.

### Priority 5 — Add features / nearbyFacilities extraction

This is useful but lower priority because it requires careful parsing. It should stay manual or semi-automatic until the core flow is stable.

Example future output:

```json
"features": ["One Gate System", "Bebas Banjir", "Siap Huni"],
"nearbyFacilities": ["Dekat Tol", "Dekat Sekolah", "Dekat Pusat Belanja"]
```

### Priority 6 — Build a real button UI

After the terminal menu works, then a simple local UI makes sense.

Possible choices:

```text
Option A: local HTML page + Python backend
Option B: Tkinter desktop app
Option C: Textual/TUI terminal UI
Option D: VS Code tasks/buttons
```

My recommendation later is **Option C or D first**, not a full web app.

The easiest “button-like” upgrade is probably **VS Code Tasks**. You can create buttons/commands inside VS Code like:

```text
Run Task: List Export Folders
Run Task: Inspect Draft
Run Task: Phase 2 Dry Run
Run Task: Validate Website
Run Task: Git Status Both Repos
```

This gives you button-like behavior without building a full app.

## Best next task

The next highest-priority development task should be:

```text
Add a safe JKPRO command menu/helper for repeated terminal commands.
```

Goal:

```text
Reduce copy-paste commands.
Avoid --latest mistakes.
Guide one listing through the safe flow.
Never apply/export without explicit confirmation.
```

I would **not** build a full UI yet. First make the command menu, prove it works, then later turn that into buttons.

## Suggested next Codex task

Use Codex to create a helper script, but only for safe workflow guidance first:

```text
Create a safe terminal helper menu for JKPRO automation.

It should:
- work only inside properti_automation-v0.3.0
- not modify website unless user chooses apply and confirms
- list Edge export folders newest first
- ask user to type exact folder name
- process exact folder name, never use --latest automatically
- inspect draft summary
- run Phase 2 dry-run
- check both repo git status
- validate image paths after apply
- print next recommended step
- use clear warnings before any destructive or write action
```

After that, your workflow becomes less like memorizing commands and more like following a guided checklist.

# you asked

message time: 2026-06-06 16:01:56

thank you and before inputting that prompt i also want to ask, how does people usually add information or listings of a product or something like into a website? and later on, if there is a listing of a property is needed to be edited or remove how would the process be like?

---

# chatgpt response

Usually there are **4 common ways** people add product/property listings to a website.

## 1. Manual code/data editing

This is what your JKPRO website currently uses.

A listing is stored in something like:

```text
data/listings.json
images/properties/<slug>/optimized/
```

To add a listing, you edit JSON and add images. This is simple, fast, cheap, and good for static websites, but it becomes tedious when there are many listings.

For your current stage, this is still good because:

```text
✅ zero budget
✅ no backend
✅ fast website
✅ safe and controlled
✅ easy Git history
```

But it needs helper tools so you do not manually type everything.

## 2. Admin dashboard / CMS

This is how many real websites do it.

There is a private admin page like:

```text
/admin
```

Then the staff fills a form:

```text
Title
Price
Location
Bedrooms
Bathrooms
Land size
Building size
Description
Agent
Images
Status
```

Then clicks:

```text
Save / Publish
```

Behind the scenes, the website saves data into a database or CMS.

Examples of CMS-style systems:

```text
WordPress
Strapi
Directus
Sanity
Payload CMS
Custom admin dashboard
```

This is convenient, but usually needs backend, login, database, security, hosting maintenance, and sometimes money.

For you, this is a **later phase**, not now.

## 3. Spreadsheet-based listing management

This is common for small teams.

Listings are managed in Google Sheets or Excel:

```text
title | price | location | type | agent | image folder | status
```

Then a script exports the sheet into website JSON.

This is actually a very good future direction for JKPRO because your office may be more comfortable with spreadsheet input than code.

Possible future flow:

```text
Google Sheet
→ validate rows
→ export data/listings.json
→ copy/optimize images
→ preview
→ deploy
```

This is easier than a full CMS, but still more structured than manual JSON editing.

## 4. Marketplace-style user submission

This is like OLX, Rumah123, 99.co, Tokopedia, Shopee, Airbnb, etc.

Users or agents log in and submit listings themselves.

This needs:

```text
user accounts
roles/permissions
image uploads
database
moderation
spam protection
security
privacy policy
admin approval
```

For your JKPRO website, I **do not recommend this yet**, because the listing source is still controlled by your office and Olga/agents. User-submitted listing is a much bigger system.

---

# For your current project, the best path is semi-automatic static publishing

Your current system is actually a good middle ground:

```text
Google Groups listing email
→ Edge extension export
→ Phase 1 draft extraction
→ human review
→ Phase 2 website export
→ preview
→ commit/tag
→ manual deploy later
```

This is not a full CMS yet, but it is much safer and cheaper.

The next improvement should be a **helper menu**, not a full admin dashboard.

Something like:

```text
JKPRO Automation Helper

1. List new export folders
2. Process selected folder
3. Inspect draft
4. Fix review fields
5. Run dry-run
6. Apply export
7. Validate website images
8. Show git status
```

This reduces command memorization without adding backend complexity.

---

# How editing a listing usually works

There are 3 types of edits.

## A. Small text/data correction

Example:

```text
fix phone number
fix location
fix floor count
fix title wording
fix price
```

Current process:

```text
edit data/listings.json
preview
commit
tag if important
```

Better future process:

```text
helper menu → update existing listing by slug → preview → commit
```

Example command later:

```text
update-listing --slug pondok-melati-001 --field floors --value 3.5
```

Or through a menu:

```text
Choose listing slug:
pondok-melati-001

Choose field:
floors

New value:
3.5
```

## B. Image update

Example:

```text
replace bad photo
add new photo
remove duplicate photo
```

Current process:

```text
edit images/properties/<slug>/optimized/
edit image paths in data/listings.json if needed
preview gallery
commit
```

Better future process:

```text
helper menu → validate images → add/remove image → regenerate image list
```

## C. Status change / remove listing

For property websites, you usually do **not hard delete immediately**. You change status first.

Common statuses:

```text
active
sold
rented
draft
hidden
archived
```

For your website, better future status values could be:

```text
for-sale
sold
rented
hidden
archived
```

So if a property is sold, instead of deleting it, you update:

```json
"status": "sold"
```

Then the website can either:

```text
show it as Sold
hide it from public listing
keep it only for internal record
```

This is safer than deleting because you keep history.

---

# Recommended future listing lifecycle for JKPRO

The best process later should be:

```text
1. New listing comes from Google Groups.
2. Extract and process it.
3. Human reviews draft.
4. Export to website as status: for-sale.
5. Preview.
6. Commit and tag.
7. Deploy manually.
8. If listing changes:
   - update price/spec/status by slug.
9. If listing is sold:
   - change status to sold or archived.
10. If listing is invalid:
   - hide/archive, not delete immediately.
```

For deletion, I recommend:

```text
First: status = hidden
Later: archive
Only delete if truly wrong/private/unsafe
```

---

# Best next development priority

I would rank the next system improvements like this:

```text
1. Add terminal helper menu for the current workflow.
2. Add update-existing-listing mode by slug.
3. Add status workflow: for-sale / sold / hidden / archived.
4. Add spreadsheet export/import later.
5. Add full admin dashboard much later.
```

So your idea about turning commands into buttons is correct, but I would do it in stages:

```text
Stage 1: terminal helper menu
Stage 2: VS Code tasks/buttons
Stage 3: simple local admin UI
Stage 4: real private web admin dashboard
```

For zero budget and safety, **Stage 1 + Stage 2** are the best next steps.

## Recommended debug/log system

For your project, there should be 3 levels of logging.

### 1. User-friendly status output

This is what the helper already started doing:

```text
Preflight passed
Draft created
Images copied
Safe to apply
All listed image files exist
```

This is for normal use. It should be readable by you, not too technical.

### 2. Debug log file

This is for troubleshooting. For example:

```text
logs/jkpro-helper-2026-06-06.log
logs/phase1-extract-2026-06-06.log
logs/phase2-export-2026-06-06.log
```

This can record:

```text
timestamp
command run
selected listing code
draft path
image count
needs_review
slug check result
location parsing result
agent mapping result
apply refused reason
error trace if something fails
```

This is very useful because if something breaks, you can copy the log and ask Codex or me to diagnose it.

### 3. Browser/devtools debug for the website

For the public website JavaScript, logs should be limited and safe.

Good browser logs:

```js
console.warn("Listing not found:", id);
console.error("Failed to load listings.json", error);
```

Avoid logging private/sensitive data like full phone lists, internal notes, raw email contents, or draft data.

For the website, debug should help with:

```text
listings.json failed to load
property id not found
image failed to load
filter/search error
missing required field
```

## What should get logs first

Highest priority places:

```text
1. Helper menu actions
2. Phase 1 processing
3. Phase 2 dry-run/apply
4. Website data loading
5. Website property detail rendering
```

More specifically:

```text
Phase 1:
- source folder selected
- draft folder created
- image count found/copied
- needs_review detected
- agent phone conflict
- filename mismatch

Phase 2:
- slug duplicate check
- location parsing result
- agent mapping result
- image path validation
- website git dirty check
- apply refused reason
- backup file created

Website:
- listings.json load success/failure
- property id missing
- missing images
- unknown type/status
```

## Best implementation style

Use Python’s built-in `logging` module for automation/helper scripts.

Good format:

```text
2026-06-06 21:45:12 INFO helper started
2026-06-06 21:45:20 INFO selected listing_code=rumah-cibubur-001
2026-06-06 21:45:24 INFO dry_run safe_to_apply=yes images=17
2026-06-06 21:45:50 WARNING apply refused reason=website_repo_dirty
2026-06-06 21:46:03 ERROR phase2 failed error=...
```

For the website JavaScript, use a tiny debug flag, for example:

```js
const DEBUG = false;
```

Then:

```js
if (DEBUG) console.log("Loaded listings:", listings.length);
```

So the public site does not become noisy.

## Why not re-extract all previous listings now?

Because re-extracting can accidentally introduce changes to already-verified listings. For example:

```text
- location parsing may change
- phone/contact might be reinterpreted
- images might be renamed or reordered
- title/description might slightly change
- previously fixed human corrections might be lost
```

Your already-exported listings are already reviewed, previewed, committed, and tagged. Better not disturb them unless there is a reason.

After we add `features`, `nearbyFacilities`, and `sellingPoints`, new exports can include them automatically or semi-automatically.

# chatgpt response

That warning means **Gemini API quota/rate limit is exhausted** for the API key Kilo Code is using.

In your screenshot, Kilo Code is trying to call:

```text
Google / Gemini Flash Latest
```

and Google returns something like:

```text
You exceeded your current quota...
```

That can happen because of one of these:

```text
1. Free Gemini API daily quota is used up.
2. Per-minute request limit was hit.
3. Token/context usage is too large.
4. Kilo Code retried several times and burned quota.
5. The selected “Gemini Flash Latest” model has stricter current limits.
6. Billing is not enabled on the Google API project.
```

Google/Gemini free access has usage limits, and recent AI free tiers can change frequently depending on model and demand. Reports also show Google has been tightening and adjusting Gemini free usage limits over time. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/ai-platforms-assistants/gemini/openai-and-google-quietly-limit-free-sora-nano-banana-pro-and-gemini-3-pro-use-heres-what-it-means-for-you?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## Best solutions for now

### 1. Wait for quota reset

This is the simplest. Free API quota often resets after a time window. Since your screenshot shows a countdown-style request stuck for many seconds, cancel it and wait.

### 2. Use a lighter model or lower settings

In Kilo Code, try:

```text
Model: Gemini Flash Lite / smaller Gemini model if available

Max tokens: lower

Task size: small
```

Avoid asking it to scan the whole project. Give it only 1–3 files or one small task.

```text

- docs update
- small test update

- suggest a small code change
```

Avoid:

- Human reviews needs_review, contact, location, enrichment fields.

- Reduce terminal typing.
- Reduce copy-paste mistakes.

- No auto deploy
- No Cloudflare upload
- No automatic commit/tag
- No deleting listings
- No bulk export
- No --latest automatic processing
- No public website admin/login system yet
- No database requirement yet

- Exact folder selection only
- Always show preflight checks
- Apply requires explicit confirmation
- Refuse if website repo is dirty
- Refuse if needs_review is not empty

- Keep logs
- Never log raw email content
- Never expose private/internal notes
- Keep backups

Stage 1: keep helper menu as backend/safety layer
Stage 2: create local desktop/web UI wrapper around helper actions
Stage 3: add draft review/edit form
Stage 4: add local preview launcher
Stage 5: later, optional Git helper buttons after proven safe
Stage 6: much later, full admin dashboard/CMS if needed

- Tkinter desktop app
- Local web UI with Python backend
- VS Code tasks/buttons
- Textual/TUI

wait before that, how about the process of rearranging an image position? like changing the front or first displayed image of the listing.

---

# chatgpt response

Yes, image order is important, because the **first image in the listing’s `images` array is usually the front/cover image** shown on the card and detail page.

Right now the process is probably:

```text
images:
1. rumah-babelan-001-001.webp  ← cover/front image
2. rumah-babelan-001-002.webp
3. rumah-babelan-001-003.webp
...
```

So to change the first displayed image, we do **not** need to rename all image files. The safer way is to **reorder the image paths inside `data/listings.json` or `draft-listing.json` before export**.

## Best process

For new listings, the ideal flow should be:

```text
1. Process exact export folder
2. Inspect draft
3. Review images
4. Choose cover image number
5. Helper reorders the image list
6. Dry-run
7. Apply
```

Example: if image `007` is the best front image, the helper could move it to the first position:

```text
Before:
001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007

After:
007, 001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006
```

The file names can stay the same. Only the JSON order changes.

## Recommended helper option to add later

This should become another helper option:

```text
15. Reorder draft images / choose cover image
```

# JKPRO Property Automation Handoff

## 1. Project Purpose

This project is for building a safer local automation workflow for JKPRO / Janlus Kaeng Propertindo property listings.

Main goal:

- Extract property listing data from Google Groups listing emails.
- Process images safely.
- Create structured draft listing JSON.
- Review and correct data with human confirmation.
- Export reviewed listings into the static JKPRO website.
- Keep the public website static, fast, privacy-safe, and easy to deploy.
- Gradually reduce terminal commands and move toward JKPRO’s own local no-terminal software.

Current priority is still **local automation + static website**, not a public CMS, not a login/admin website, and not automatic Cloudflare deployment.

## 6. Current Workflow

### Export source

Google Groups listing emails are extracted using the Edge extension.

Export folder root:

```powershell
D:\Downloads (D)\JKPRO-Extracts
```

Example export folders:

```text
rumah-babelan-001

rumah-jaksel-001
```

### Start helper

From automation repo:

```powershell
cd "D:\Documents (D)\Softwares\test website\properti-projects\properti_automation-v0.3.0"
python scripts\jkpro_helper.py
```

Current helper menu after v0.6.0:

```text
1. Show git status for both repos
2. List newest Edge extension export folders
3. Process an exact export folder name through Phase 1
4. Inspect a draft summary
5. Run Phase 2 dry-run for a selected draft
6. Apply Phase 2 export only after explicit confirmation
7. Validate latest website listing image paths
8. Print safe next-step checklist
9. Exit
10. Edit draft review fields
11. Edit draft location/title
12. Edit draft enrichment fields
13. Fix latest website m2 encoding
14. Show latest website listing JSON summary
```

### Normal safe workflow

```text
1. Use Edge extension on one Google Groups listing.
2. Verify export folder exists and is newest.
3. Run helper.
4. Option 1: check both repos are clean.
5. Option 2: list export folders.
6. Option 3: process exact export folder.
7. Option 4: inspect draft summary.
8. Option 10: edit draft review fields if needed.
9. Option 11: edit title/location if needed.
10. Option 12: edit enrichment fields if needed.
11. Option 5: Phase 2 dry-run.
12. If dry-run is clean, option 6: apply with exact APPLY confirmation.
13. Option 7: validate latest image paths.
14. Option 13: fix m² encoding if needed.
15. Option 14: inspect latest website JSON summary.
16. Preview local website.
17. Commit website export.
18. Tag website export.
19. Check both repos clean.
```

## 7. Safety Rules

Always follow these rules:

```text
- Never use --latest automatically unless newest folder was verified first.
- Always process an exact folder/listing code.
- Never bulk export.
- Never auto-deploy.
- Never auto-publish to Cloudflare.
- Never auto-commit/tag from helper.
- Never edit real website data without preview/checks.
- Never apply Phase 2 if needs_review is not empty.
- Never apply if website repo is dirty.
- Never apply if slug/image folder already exists.
- Always validate JSON after apply.
- Always validate image paths.
- Always preview locally before website commit.
- Keep terminal/helper workflow as backup even after future UI exists.
```

## 10. Location Parsing Lessons

### Bogor

v0.5.5 added support for Bogor / Kabupaten Bogor parsing.

Example:

```text
KOMPLEK AL CIANGSANA GUNUNG PUTRI BOGOR
```

Target:

```text
location: Komplek Al Ciangsana Gunung Putri, Bogor
locationArea: Komplek Al Ciangsana Gunung Putri
locationCity: Bogor
province: Jawa Barat
```

### Kabupaten Bekasi

v0.5.10 added support for Kabupaten Bekasi.

Important reason:

```text
Kota Bekasi and Kabupaten Bekasi must be distinct.
“Bekasi” alone is often understood as Kota Bekasi.
“Kabupaten Bekasi” must stay explicit.
```

Example:

```text
UJUNG HARAPAN BAHAGIA BABELAN KABUPATEN BEKASI
```

Target:

```text
location: Ujung Harapan Bahagia Babelan, Kabupaten Bekasi
locationArea: Ujung Harapan Bahagia Babelan
locationCity: Kabupaten Bekasi
province: Jawa Barat
```

### Kota Bekasi

Example:

```text
CIKETING MUSTIKA JAYA KOTA BEKASI
```

Target:

```text
location: Ciketing Mustika Jaya, Kota Bekasi
locationArea: Ciketing Mustika Jaya
locationCity: Kota Bekasi
province: Jawa Barat
```

## 12. Enrichment Field Strategy

v0.5.9 added optional support for:

```text
features
nearbyFacilities
sellingPoints
```

Updated meaning after review:

### features

Property/building/unit/spec-related advantages.

Examples:

```text
Carport 1 mobil
Akses 2 mobil
Dimensi 6 x 12 m²
Bangunan tahun 2016
Fully furnished
Parkir masuk container 40 ft
```

### sellingPoints

Marketing advantages / “Keunggulan”.

Examples:

```text
Lokasi sangat strategis
Dekat Tol Jatiwarna & Shuttle Bus
Dekat ke Tol Jatiasih, Tol Becakayu, Jatiwaringin, Tol Jatibening
Bebas banjir
One gate system
Security 24 jam
Cocok untuk investasi
Occupancy 95-100%
Net income Rp 37,3 Juta / bulan
ROI 9-12% / tahun
```

Important update:

```text
Bebas banjir should go under sellingPoints / Keunggulan.
```

### nearbyFacilities

Nearby public facilities or landmarks.

Examples:

```text
Sekolah
Rumah sakit
Pusat perbelanjaan
Rumah ibadah
Kantor pemerintahan
Kuliner
SPBU
Gerai ATM
Curug Cilember
Taman Wisata Matahari
Cimory Riverside
Air Terjun Bidadari
```

```text
Spesifikasi
```

```text
Deskripsi
Spesifikasi
```

```text
Data Investasi if applicable
Keunggulan & Fasilitas Sekitar
```

## 14. Example Data Extraction Rules by Property Type

### Rumah

Preserve:

```text
land_area_m2
building_area_m2
bedrooms
bathrooms
floors
carport
garage
orientation
dimension
electricity
water_source
accessRoad
terraceBalcony
certificate_type
```

Selling points:

```text
Lokasi sangat strategis
Detailed toll access
Shuttle bus
Bebas banjir
One gate system
```

### Ruko

Rules:

```text
property_type = ruko
bedrooms = null if not present
bathrooms from source
floors can be decimal, e.g. 3.5
furnishing can be Unfurnished
```

Important:

```text
If title says 4LT but SPESIFIKASI says 3,5, structured spec follows SPESIFIKASI.
```

### Apartemen

Rules:

```text
property_type = apartemen
land_area_m2 = null
building_area_m2 = unit area
unitFloor for “Lantai 5”
parking instead of carport if possible
legalitas SHGB or SHGB/SHMSRS if source says so
```

Apartment display:

```text
Garasi / Carport 1 Mobil -> Parkir 1 mobil
```

### Tanah

Rules:

```text
property_type = tanah
building_area_m2 = null
bedrooms = null
bathrooms = null
floors = null
carport = null
garage = null
```

Preserve:

```text
price per m²
total price
land shape
dimension
suitable uses
investment potential
```

### Gudang

Rules:

```text
property_type = gudang
bedrooms = null
bathrooms can be present
building area may have formula, e.g. 1.500 m² x 2 bangunan
```

Preserve commercial details:

```text
Office terpisah
Container 40 ft access/parking
Kios disewakan
Indomaret
Security 24 jam
```

### Gedung Kantor

Rules:

```text
property_type = gedung_kantor
buildingFacilities should not be mixed with nearbyFacilities
```

Preserve:

```text
Rooftop / helipad
Hydrant
Fire alarm
Lift
Pantry
Granite
Parking count
Suitable business uses
```

### Hotel

Rules:

```text
property_type = hotel
hotel room count is not normal bedrooms
two SPESIFIKASI sections should be merged
LOKASI DEKAT KE should be preserved as nearby attractions
FASILITAS should become buildingFacilities / fasilitas properti
```

Preserve:

```text
bungalows
hotelRooms
meetingRooms
meetingRoomCapacities
pool
billiard
table tennis
kolam mancing
danau luas
```

### Kontrakan

Rules:

```text
property_type = kontrakan
unit count matters
monthly income matters
```

If title and spec conflict:

```text
title: Kontrakan 4 Pintu
spec: Kontrakan 5 Pintu
```

Add:

```text
needs_review: unit_count_conflict
```

### Kost

Rules:

```text
property_type = kost
This is investment data, not normal house bedroom data.
```

Preserve:

```text
room count
occupancy
net income
ROI
room price range
additional income potential
furnishing
facilities
survey note
```

Do not display as normal:

```text
Kamar Tidur 35
```

Better:

```text
Kamar Kost: 34 + 1
```

Income/ROI claims should trigger human review.

## 15. Discussed Example Extraction Patterns

### Babelan house

Source:

```text
RUMAH SECOND DIJUAL MURAH LOKASI STRATEGIS DI UJUNG HARAPAN BAHAGIA BABELAN KAB BEKASI
```

Final target:

```text
location: Ujung Harapan Bahagia Babelan, Kabupaten Bekasi
sellingPoints:
- One gate system
- Lokasi sangat strategis
- Dekat tol
- Bebas banjir
nearbyFacilities:
- Sekolah
- Rumah sakit
- Pusat perbelanjaan
- Rumah ibadah
- Kantor pemerintahan
- Kuliner
- SPBU
- Gerai ATM
```

### Cikunir / Jakamulya house

Important selling points:

```text
Dekat Tol Jatiwarna & Shuttle Bus
Dekat ke Tol Jatiasih, Tol Becakayu, Jatiwaringin, Tol Jatibening
Bebas banjir
```

These should not be compressed to only `Dekat Tol`.

### Pondok Melati ruko

Important:

```text
property_type = ruko
floors = 3.5
display: 3,5
Dekat Tol Jatiwarna & Shuttle Bus
Dekat ke Tol Jatiasih
Dekat ke Tol Kota Wisata
Bebas banjir
```

### Mall BTC apartment

Important:

```text
property_type = apartemen
unitFloor = 5
parking = 1
furnishing = Fully furnished
furnishingItems should preserve all included items
Swimming pool should be sellingPoint / facility
```

### Ciketing land

Important:

```text
price_unit = per_m2
price_number = 6000000
total_price_number = 7200000000
locationCity = Kota Bekasi
```

### Kosambi warehouse

Important:

```text
property_type = gudang
building_area_m2 = 3000
building_area_note = 1.500 m² x 2 bangunan
total_price_number = 52272000000
```

Preserve:

```text
Parkir masuk container 40 ft
Office terpisah
Kios disewakan
Indomaret
```

### Pondok Pinang office building

Important:

```text
property_type = gedung_kantor
locationCity = Jakarta Selatan
province = DKI Jakarta
buildingFacilities separate from nearbyFacilities
```

Potential typo review:

```text
Tol Sinatupang probably should be Tol Simatupang, but confirm before changing.
```

### Puncak Cisarua hotel

Important:

```text
property_type = hotel
land_area_m2 = 23000
building_area_m2 = 2000
hotelRooms = 45
bungalows = 15
meetingRooms = 3
meetingRoomCapacities = 50, 100, 250
```

### Kebalen Babelan kontrakan

Important conflict:

```text
title says 4 pintu
spec says 5 pintu
needs_review: unit_count_conflict
```

### Harapan Kita Kelapa Dua kost

Important:

```text
property_type = kost
price = Rp 4,9 Miliar
locationCity = Tangerang
province = Banten
roomCount = 34
extraRoomCount = 1
occupancy = 95-100%
netIncomeMonthly = 37300000
ROI = 9-12% / tahun
```

Income/ROI claims need human review.
